topic: Texas option period: 10 paper days vs 6 real days
hook: You paid for 10 option days. You got 6.

scores.worst_problem: The hook already states the arithmetic (10 becomes 6), so slide 4's reveal lands as confirmation rather than payoff and the middle slides lose tension.
scores.fix: Either withhold the number in the hook ("You paid for 10 option days. You will not get 10.") or make slide 4 deliver something the hook didn't — a cost figure or the one day nobody counts.

deck.topic: Texas option period: 10 paper days vs 6 real days
deck.hook: You paid for 10 option days. You got 6.

points.title: The Clock Starts Quietly
body: Your option period starts the day after everyone signs.
Nobody calls to tell you it began.
points.loop: And you are not first in line.

points.title: Good Inspectors Are Booked
body: The ones worth hiring are three days out.
Take whoever is free today and you get what you pay for.
points.loop: The report is only half the job.

points.title: A Report Is Not A Number
body: Sellers negotiate off real bids, not off scary sentences.
Getting a contractor out to quote it takes another day or two.
points.loop: Now count what is actually left.

points.title: Ten Becomes Six
body: One day burns on signatures and getting your option fee delivered.
Three more sit waiting on the inspector.
Ten on paper. Six in real life.
points.loop: Day six has a trap in it.

points.title: 5PM Is Not A Suggestion
body: The deadline is a time, not a date.
Notice has to be delivered by then, not decided by then.
points.loop: You can win those days back.

linkedinCaption:
A 10 day option period in Texas is rarely 10 usable days.

The clock starts the day after execution. No one calls to tell you it began. One day goes to signatures and delivering the option fee. Good inspectors are often booked three days out, and the ones available same day are usually available for a reason. Then the report lands, and a report is not a number. Sellers negotiate off contractor bids, which takes another day or two to arrange.

Ten on paper. Closer to six in practice. And the deadline is 5PM, a time and not a date. Notice must be delivered by then.

For the agents here: how early do you line up your inspector, and do you book before the contract is fully executed?
